name: Flint (nodular chalcedony from the chalk), freshly broken

diffuseAlbedo.source: M. M. Aliyu, W. Murphy, J. A. Lawrence, R. Collier, 'Engineering geological characterization of flints', QJEGH 50(2), 133-147, 2017 (accepted version, https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/111092/1/aliyu%20et%20al%202017.pdf), Table 1: dark brown grey flint (DBG) 5YR 2/1; Table 2: DBG in the Seaford Chalk (East Sussex, Dieppe) and Lewes Chalk (Mesnil-Val); Munsell renotation real.dat (RIT MCSL): 5YR 2/2 x 0.3880, y 0.3476, Y 3.126
diffuseAlbedo.note: real.dat has no chroma-1 entry, so the halfway interpolation is approximate. Other Table 1 classes: GF N5, LBG 5YR 6/1, BG 5G 2/1. Aliyu's grey flints are from the Northern Province Burnham Chalk. The old N3 converts to L* about 30.8. The stage calls the inside 'glassy black', which agrees with this darker value.
diffuseAlbedo.derivation: Chroma 1 taken halfway in xy between illuminant C (0.3101, 0.3162) and 5YR 2/2, giving (0.3491, 0.3319) at Y 0.03126. Bradford adaptation C to D65, then CIELAB D65. I recomputed this independently and got [20.5, 3.9, 4.2].

refractiveIndex.source: S. Md. Shahabudden, N. Sultana, 'Physical and optical properties of chalcedony gemstone - a case study from Kolluru area, Guntur District, Andhra Pradesh, India', JETIR 7(4), 2020, https://www.jetir.org/papers/JETIR2004235.pdf, Table 5.10: refractometer RI 1.534-1.540 across 23 samples, SG 2.58-2.62
refractiveIndex.derivation: The middle of the measured 1.534 to 1.540
refractiveIndex.note: Measured on Indian chalcedony varieties (carnelian, agate, jasper, plasma), not on chalk flint. Flint's microcrystalline quartz, moganite and water put it below quartz's 1.547, which is consistent. A low-tier journal.

porosity.source: R. Mortimore, 'Flints in the Late Cretaceous Chalk of NW Europe', Deposits Magazine, 17 July 2020, https://depositsmag.com/2020/07/17/flints-in-the-late-cretaceous-chalk-of-nw-europe/: interior of flint 'up to 1% to 5% porosity', cortex '3% to 12%' (Lautridou et al. 1986); Aliyu et al. 2017 Tables 6 and 9: DBG (Seaford/Lewes) density 2.66-2.69 Mg/m3, silica over 99 %
porosity.derivation: A value in the lower part of the 1 to 5 % interior range, chosen for the dense, over-99 %-silica southern DBG flints
porosity.note: Correction to the derivation: Aliyu's caliper densities of 2.66 to 2.69 exceed quartz's 2.65, so they cannot resolve porosity at the percent level. They show only that the flint is dense. 0.02 is a judgement inside Lautridou's range. This is the broken interior; the cortex is 3 to 12 %.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: Mortimore 2020, Deposits Magazine (URL above): flint has 'a very fine-grained structure (size of grains 0.5-20 um)'
grain.note: The value is unchanged, now with a source.
grain.derivation: 10 um lies inside the 0.5 to 20 um range

bed.source: Docs/Stages/cube.md section 7, 'Flint nodule bands': 'nodules r 0.06-0.12 in a 0.24 cell' (read, line 346)
bed.note: A design value. It is a radius: the largest nodule is 240 mm across, the same as the cell.
bed.derivation: The largest nodule radius of the stage rule, 0.12 m

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the topsoil's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
